A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BITS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, retrieval, dense prediction, domain adaptation, ablation, and representation-analysis results in Section 5 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds soft-target distribution measurements and an evaluated hybrid method in Appendices A and E.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces an optional iBOT-style hybrid that adds a patch-level binary cross-entropy objective with 8-bit targets. This is a limited procedural extension of the retained BITS teacher–student method. The coding-rate formula also replaces d with B; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: No additional dataset, domain, or downstream task is reported. Appendix E evaluates ImageNet-1K classification and retrieval, already covered in v1; the existing transfer benchmarks and qualitative examples remain.

E2.justification: V1 explicitly excludes DINOv2 comparisons, whereas v2 evaluates DINOv2 in Appendix E, Table 15. Existing DINO and SimDINO comparisons remain. The iBOT-style hybrid is a proposed variant, not an evaluated original iBOT baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a diagnostic measuring soft-target fractions above 0.99 and below 0.01 at temperatures 0.1 and 0.01. Appendix E evaluates an additional 8-bit-per-patch hybrid configuration. Existing training budgets and evaluation metrics are retained; the new comparison's full training settings are not specified.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds quantitative target-distribution analysis to test whether successful low-temperature soft targets are nearly binary. Appendix E also explores complementarity with patch-level supervision. The original component ablations, training curves, domain-shift analyses, and qualitative studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new target-distribution percentages are descriptive findings, not a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–14 and existing figure results are unchanged. New Table 15 reports DINOv2 at 38.33/75.93/76.8 and the hybrid at 47.03/76.66/78 for mAP/k-NN/linear probing; these are added comparisons, not established same-setting gains. Appendix A adds target proportions above 0.99/below 0.01: 48.33%/48.25% at temperature 0.1 and 49.66%/49.99% at 0.01.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds explicit entropy and mutual-information bounds, H(Z) <= B and I(Z1; Z2) <= B, with accompanying reasoning. The coding-rate expression changes from d/epsilon^2 in v1 Equation 9 to B/epsilon^2 in v2 Equation 10, aligning the factor with the channel dimension.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about discrete communication, factorized representations, periodic head resets, and downstream performance. The added appendix findings do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds a hypothesis connecting factorization to easier domain adaptation in Section 5.4 and explicitly identifies the untested extension beyond ViT-B/16 in Section 5.6. Appendix E suggests compatibility with patch-level losses while acknowledging that the DINOv2 comparison does not match all training factors.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies limited technical information for the new hybrid: binary cross-entropy and 8 bits per patch. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures remain. Detailed hybrid loss weighting, training schedules, and additional resource-access information are not provided.

R1.justification: V2 adds Locatello et al. (2019) to support its discussion of entangled representations and domain adaptation. Appendix E expands positioning relative to DINOv2 and iBOT-style patch objectives; the main related-work section otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds a capacity discussion, a limitations subsection, and Appendix E, with localized wording changes and updated publication, correspondence, and equal-contribution information.

P2.justification: V2 adds a pipeline diagram as Figure 1 and the comparison table as Table 15. Existing figures retain their content and are renumbered, with local figure/table relocation and text reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity through the pipeline figure and mathematical correction, strengthens the soft-target explanation with measurements, and explicitly states scale and comparison limitations. The new hybrid and DINOv2 results provide useful context, but unmatched and incompletely specified training factors limit their evidential strength. These are modest gains over an otherwise unchanged core empirical study.
